title: You didn’t reject the title…
paragraphs:
You didn’t reject the title…
you rejected what it can turn you into.
And that’s where it gets uncomfortable.

Because some people wear “pastor” like a crown—
but you’ve seen how quickly a crown can become a cover.

You’ve seen sermons louder than their secret life.
Prayers that sound holy… but hearts that drift quietly.
Hands raised in public… while compromise grows in private.
So you stepped back.

Not because you don’t love God.
But because you fear becoming something fake.
But here’s the tension you can’t escape:

What if your refusal isn’t just humility…
what if part of it is protection?

Protection from expectation.
From accountability.
From the weight of being seen.

Because once people recognize the calling,
you can’t hide in the crowd anymore.
And deep down…
you know that.
Let me ask you something you won’t hear often:

Are you avoiding the title…
or avoiding the responsibility that comes with it?
Selah.

Because Ephesians 4:11 says God gave shepherds to His church—not to elevate them, but to equip people.
And 1 Peter 5:2–3 doesn’t say “be called a shepherd”… it says be one—willingly, eagerly, as an example.
So the issue was never the title.
It’s the heart behind it.
Read that again.
Here’s the AHA moment most people miss:

You can reject a title publicly…
and still crave recognition privately.
That’s the quieter pride.

The one that whispers,
“I’m different. I’m not like them.”

But humility doesn’t announce itself.
And it definitely doesn’t compare.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:

You’re not uncomfortable with the title.
You’re uncomfortable with what God might require if you accept who you really are.
And here’s where it gets piercing:
Some people hide behind titles.
But others hide behind the absence of one.
Both can be masks.
Jesus never fought for a title.

In fact, Philippians 2:6–7 shows He emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant.
Yet heaven still called Him Lord.
He didn’t chase recognition.
But He never ran from responsibility either.
So where does that leave you?
Right here.
At the crossroads between calling and comfort.
Between anonymity and obedience.

Between staying safe…
or stepping into what God is clearly forming in you.
Because the truth is:
You don’t need to be called “pastor” to shepherd people.

But if you are shepherding…
you are accountable to the Chief Shepherd.

Hebrews 13:17 speaks of leaders who will give an account.
Not for titles they held—
but for souls they handled.
That’s weight.
Holy weight.
Conviction line:

God is not impressed by how well you avoid titles…
He is watching how faithfully you carry responsibility.
But here’s the grace.
And don’t miss this.
You don’t have to become a perfect leader.
You just have to become a surrendered one.

Because the Gospel was never about qualified men—
it was about called sinners redeemed by Jesus.
Romans 5:8 reminds us: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

Not when you were ready.
Not when you had a title.
But right in your mess.
So if part of you fears failure…
Good.
That means you know you can’t do this without Him.
And that’s exactly where grace flows.
Identity shift:

You are not a man trying to avoid a title.
You are a servant being shaped for responsibility.

You are not protecting your image.
You are being invited into obedience.
And obedience will always cost more than comfort.
But it will also lead you closer to Christ.
So what now?
Search your heart.
Not your label.
Lay down both pride and fear.

Say, “Lord, I don’t want the title…
but I won’t run from the calling.”
That’s the prayer that changes everything.
And if God is peeling back layers in your life, stay close.
Follow if you’re ready to grow.

And the next message…
it’s going to confront the one thing you still haven’t surrendered.
